steps: Carbon monoxide (CO) combines with haemoglobin in the blood and reduces its ability to carry oxygen. In high concentration, it may cause suffocation and death.
Sulphur dioxide (SO₂) irritates the respiratory system and causes breathing problems. It also contributes to acid rain, which damages plants and buildings.
Nitrogen oxides (NOₓ) irritate the lungs and cause respiratory problems. They contribute to photochemical smog and acid rain.
Unburnt hydrocarbons help form photochemical smog; some are harmful to health and may cause cancer.
Particulate matter, such as dust and smoke, enters the respiratory system and can cause breathing difficulties and lung diseases.
Chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs) damage the ozone layer, allowing more harmful ultraviolet radiation to reach the Earth.
items.finalAnswer: Major air pollutants harm human health, damage plants and buildings, and pollute the atmosphere.
